name: Civil unrest
summary: Police held 154 after Yogyakarta protests on 10 Nov; unrest goes on in Pakistani Kashmir; no nationwide deadly unrest
state: Police in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, used tear gas and water cannon on protesters on 10 Nov and said they detained 154 people; rights groups called for an inquiry into alleged excessive force, and a legal aid group said 13 people were unreachable on 11 Nov (Jakarta Post; Malay Mail). In Pakistan-administered Kashmir, unrest continued after the 5 Nov clearance of Rawalakot protest camps, and police said a Rangers officer died on 8 Nov (Express Tribune, 9 Nov). No deadly nationwide unrest was found.
for_you: Protests can disrupt travel at short notice. Check FCDO travel advice for Indonesia and Pakistan before travelling, and avoid demonstrations as it advises.
rubric_hit: Significant protests in several countries and deadly unrest in one (Watch); no deadly nationwide unrest

sources.title: The Jakarta Post — Yogyakarta crackdown leaves dozens unreachable
Malay Mail — Indonesia police deploy tear gas, water cannon in Yogyakarta unrest, detain 154
Express Tribune — TTAP calls for immediate end to violence, resumption of talks to quell AJK unrest

why: Mass protest and state crackdowns signal political fragility and can topple governments.
drivers: Cost of living, elections, corruption, repression, food and fuel prices.

rubric.alert: Deadly nationwide unrest or a state crackdown in a major country.
rubric.watch: Significant protests in several countries or deadly unrest in one.
rubric.normal: No deadly mass unrest in large countries.
